The von Mises Tails Below the Series' Resolution

Source: R/vonmises1_distrib.R
vm_cdf_tail.Rd

vm_cdf_tail() returns \(P(Y \le q)\) or \(P(Y > q)\), or their logarithms, from the series of vm_cdf() where the requested tail is above \(10^{-6}\), and from vm_log_tail() below. The series has an absolute error of about \(10^{-16}\), which grows slowly with \(\kappa\), so below that threshold its relative error would exceed about \(10^{-9}\). vm_log_tail() integrates \(e^{\kappa\cos(y - \mu)}\) over the tail, which excludes the mode, so the integrand decreases from each end of the interval to the antimode. The interval is split at the antimode when it contains it, and each piece is integrated from its end on the scale \(1/\max\{\kappa|\sin(e - \mu)|, \sqrt\kappa\}\) at that end \(e\), relative to the value there, over panels of growing width until the remainder is below \(10^{-17}\) of the sum. The difference of the cosines is written as a product of sines. The pieces are added on the log scale, and the normalizing constant comes from numericals7::log_bessel_i(), so that the factors do not underflow at any concentration.

Usage

vm_log_tail(q, mu, kappa, lower)

vm_log_piece(e, dir, L, mu, kappa)

vm_cdf_tail(q, mu, kappa, lower.tail, log.p)

Arguments

q

A numeric vector of angles in \([-\pi, \pi)\).

mu, kappa

Numeric vectors, the mean direction and the concentration.

lower, lower.tail, log.p

Logical of length 1.

e, dir, L

For vm_log_piece(), which integrates one piece: the end \(e\) at which the integrand is largest, the direction (1 or -1) in which it decreases, and the length of the piece.

Value

A numeric vector for vm_cdf_tail(); for vm_log_tail() and vm_log_piece(), a number, the logarithm of the tail probability and of the integral of \(e^{\kappa\cos(y - \mu)}\) over the piece.

Examples

distributions7:::vm_cdf_tail(-1, 0, 100, TRUE, FALSE)
#> [1] 5.101678e-22
